mainTopic: Making up a missed מנחה and missing הבדלה in the עמידה; whether the תפילות come from the אבות or match the תמידין, and רבי יהודה's prayer deadlines
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about someone who forgot מנחה on ערב שבת or on שבת. He makes it up with a second עמידה at the next prayer. On מוצאי שבת, הבדלה goes only in the first עמידה. The גמרא infers that an עמידה without הבדלה does not count. A תוספתא says we do not send him back for missing הבדלה, because he can say it over wine, and this contradiction stays a קשיא. Next comes a מחלוקת: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the אבות instituted the תפילות, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says they match the תמידין. A ברייתא supports each view. The second ties every prayer's time to its offering, including רבי יהודה's earlier deadlines, and defines מנחה גדולה and מנחה קטנה. The גמרא shows that רבי יהודה's פלג המנחה is the midpoint of the later period. It then answers that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא is not refuted: the אבות instituted the prayers and the חכמים linked them to the offerings, as מוסף shows. The amud ends by asking whether רבי יהודה's 'until four hours' includes the fourth hour, and the proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Making up a missed מנחה around שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who forgot מנחה on ערב שבת or on שבת makes it up by praying two עמידות at the next prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: If someone made a mistake and did not pray מנחה on Friday afternoon, he prays two עמידות on Friday night. If someone made a mistake and did not pray מנחה on שבת, he prays two weekday עמידות on מוצאי שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that explains how to make up a missed מנחה when the next prayer falls on a different kind of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The makeup prayer follows the type of the prayer he is saying now, not the day he missed. On Friday night both עמידות are שבת prayers. On מוצאי שבת both are weekday prayers, even though the missed מנחה was on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught.' This introduces a ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה.
He erred, meaning he forgot by mistake.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he erred and did not pray the afternoon prayer
on Friday (the eve of Shabbat),
he prays two on Friday night.
If he erred and did not pray the afternoon prayer on Shabbat,
he prays on Saturday night
two weekday Amidas.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A missed מנחה is made up with a second עמידה at the next prayer, and that second עמידה follows the type of day of the current prayer.

steps.title: Where to say הבדלה when making up the prayer on מוצאי שבת
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא continues: הבדלה goes in the first עמידה only. If he put it in the second instead, only the second counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says הבדלה (אתה חוננתנו) in the first עמידה, and he does not say it in the second. If he said it in the second and not in the first, the second counts for him and the first does not count for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going and adds a detail about הבדלה for the person praying two עמידות on מוצאי שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first עמידה is the real מעריב, so it is the one that gets הבדלה. The second is only a makeup for the missed שבת מנחה, so it gets no הבדלה. If he switched them, the ברייתא says the first one does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: He says הבדלה, which marks the line between שבת and the weekday. In the עמידה this is אתה חוננתנו.
The first and the second עמידה.
It counted for him; he fulfilled his obligation with it.

steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling that the first עמידה 'did not count' is the line the גמרא is about to analyze and challenge.

phrases.english: He says havdala in the first,
and he does not say havdala in the second.
And if he said havdala in the second
and did not say havdala in the first,
the second counted for him,
the first did not count for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַבְדִּיל בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the הבדלה detail.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הבדלה goes in the first עמידה only. If it was said only in the second, the first does not count.

steps.title: Inference: missing הבדלה means the prayer must be repeated
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא means that an עמידה without הבדלה is like no prayer at all, so he must repeat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that since he did not say הבדלה in the first, it is as if he did not pray at all, and we send him back to pray again?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from the ברייתא's words 'the first did not count.' It is setting up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the first עמידה did not count, and the only thing missing from it was הבדלה. So the גמרא infers a general rule: whoever leaves out הבדלה in the עמידה must repeat it. This rule will now be tested against another source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that to say?' This draws a conclusion from a source, often in order to challenge it.
He is considered like one who did not pray.
We make him go back and repeat.

phrases.english: Is that to say that since
he did not say havdala in the first,
he is like one who did not pray,
and we make him go back and repeat?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּכֵיוָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule out of the last line of the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does leaving out הבדלה in the עמידה make it invalid, so that it must be repeated?

steps.title: Contradiction: another source says we do not send him back for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: A תוספתא says that rain-mentions forgotten in the עמידה require repeating, but forgotten הבדלה does not, because it can be said over a cup of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it with this: If someone erred and did not mention the power of rain (משיב הרוח) in תחיית המתים, or the request for rain in ברכת השנים, we make him go back. But for הבדלה in חונן הדעת, we do not make him go back, because he can say it over the cup of wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different source that directly contradicts the inference it just made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תוספתא openly says that missing הבדלה in the עמידה does not require repeating, since one can make it up with הבדלה over wine. That clashes with the inference from the ברייתא that the prayer without הבדלה 'did not count.' Rain is different because there is no other way to make it up.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted them.' This introduces a contradicting source.
Mentioning the power of rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם) in the second ברכה.
Asking for rain (ותן טל ומטר) in ברכת השנים.
We make him go back and repeat.
Over the cup of wine, meaning the separate הבדלה ceremony.

phrases.english: And they contrasted it:
If he erred and did not mention the power of rain
in the blessing of the revival of the dead,
or the request for rain in the blessing of the years,
we make him go back.
Havdala in 'Who graciously grants knowledge':
we do not make him go back,
because he can say it over the cup!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference of step 3 with a contradicting source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that an עמידה without הבדלה does not count and must be repeated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תוספתא explicitly rules that we do not send him back for missing הבדלה, since he can fulfill it over wine.

steps.title: The contradiction stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא declares the contradiction a קשיא, a difficulty with no answer given.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a difficulty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the contradiction and moves on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word קשיא does not end a position completely. It means the two sources clash and the גמרא offers no resolution. Both sources remain on the table without being reconciled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is difficult.' The question stands unanswered, which is weaker than a full refutation (תיובתא).

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא suggests that an עמידה without הבדלה does not count. The תוספתא says we do not send him back for missing הבדלה, since he can say it over wine. The גמרא leaves this as an unresolved קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: קשיא here does not mean one source is thrown out. It only means the גמרא could not reconcile them in this sugya.

phrases.english: It is a difficulty.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The contradiction about whether missing הבדלה requires repeating the עמידה is left unresolved.

steps.title: First view: the אבות instituted the prayers
steps.stepSummary: A new topic opens. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the three daily תפילות were instituted by the אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: The prayers were instituted by the אבות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about where the three daily prayers come from, opening with the first side of a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this view, the source of the daily prayers is the practice of אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב. That would make prayer older than the בית המקדש offerings and independent of them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was stated.' This introduces a statement or a dispute of the אמוראים.
The prayers, meaning the daily עמידות.
The Patriarchs: אברהם, יצחק, and יעקב.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
The prayers, the Patriarchs instituted them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new sugya, unrelated to the הבדלה contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daily prayers were instituted by the אבות.

steps.title: Second view: the prayers match the daily offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees and says the תפילות were instituted to correspond to the תמידין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The prayers were instituted to correspond to the daily תמיד offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the מחלוקת, which sets up the discussion that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here prayer is modeled on the קרבנות of the בית המקדש. This view would explain prayer times by the times of the offerings. The גמרא will next bring sources for each view.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offerings brought in the בית המקדש every morning and afternoon.

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת is the background for the dispute in the משנה about the deadlines for each prayer.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The prayers were instituted corresponding to the daily offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing side of the מחלוקת opened in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daily prayers were instituted to correspond to the תמידין.

steps.title: Introducing support for both views
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא supports each of the two earlier views.
steps.simpleTranslation: A teaching supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, and a teaching supports רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: it will present a source for each view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two views remain distinct. This line does not yet explain either source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in an earlier teaching.
The sage who linked the prayers to the אבות.
The sage who linked the prayers to the תְּמִידִין.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא,
phrases.english: It was taught in support of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina,

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי.
phrases.english: and it was taught in support of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא moves from רבי יהושע בן לוי’s view to an announcement that both views have supporting teachings.

steps.title: A morning prayer linked to אַבְרָהָם
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports the link between אַבְרָהָם and שַׁחֲרִית by reading his morning standing as prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A teaching supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: אַבְרָהָם established the morning prayer. A verse places him standing early in the morning, and another verse uses standing for prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins the first supporting ברייתא. It shows why the verse about אַבְרָהָם can be read as describing morning prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse supplies the morning time and the word “stood.” The verse about פִּינְחָס connects standing with prayer.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: It was taught in support of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina:
Abraham instituted the morning prayer,
as it is stated: “And Abraham rose early in the morning
to the place where he had stood.”
And “standing” here means prayer,
as it is stated: “And Pinehas stood and prayed.”

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא now presents the first of the two sources it announced.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse places אַבְרָהָם standing in the morning; the verse about פִּינְחָס connects standing with prayer.

steps.title: An afternoon prayer linked to יִצְחָק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא links יִצְחָק to מִנְחָה through a verse about going out to speak toward evening.
steps.simpleTranslation: יִצְחָק established the afternoon prayer. A verse says he went out to converse toward evening, and another verse uses that kind of speech for prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its second example, connecting יִצְחָק to afternoon prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: “Toward evening” supplies the time. The second verse explains why the word for speaking can be understood as prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: Speech or conversation; here interpreted as prayer.

phrases.english: Isaac instituted the afternoon prayer,
as it is stated: “And Isaac went out to converse in the field
toward evening.”
And “conversation” here means prayer,
as it is stated: “A prayer of the afflicted when he is faint,
and he pours out his speech before the Lord.”

steps.triggerLanguage: יִצְחָק תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת מִנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא applies the same kind of verse-based reading to the second daily prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse about יִצְחָק supplies the time and the word for speaking; the verse about the afflicted person connects that speech with prayer.

steps.title: An evening prayer linked to יַעֲקֹב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא links יַעֲקֹב to עַרְבִית by reading his encounter as prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: יַעֲקֹב established the evening prayer. A verse says he encountered the place and stayed there overnight; another verse uses “encounter” alongside prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its third example, connecting יַעֲקֹב to evening prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about יַעֲקֹב places the event when he stayed overnight. The verse containing “do not encounter Me” connects the word for encounter with praying.
steps.whatToRemember: The first ברייתא connects each of the three daily תְּפִלּוֹת to an אָב through a verse about his action and a second verse that identifies that action with prayer.

phrases.english: Jacob instituted the evening prayer,
as it is stated: “And he encountered the place
and stayed there overnight.”
And “encounter” here means prayer,
as it is stated: “And you, do not pray
on behalf of this people, and do not raise

phrases.aramaic: בַעֲדָם רִנָּה וּתְפִלָּה וְאַל תִּפְגַּע בִּי״
phrases.english: song or prayer on their behalf, and do not encounter Me.”

steps.triggerLanguage: יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא completes its three examples supporting רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse about יַעֲקֹב supplies the overnight setting; the later verse uses the word for encounter alongside words for prayer.

steps.title: The morning prayer’s endpoint follows the offering
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא explains the noon endpoint for morning prayer through the morning תָּמִיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A teaching supports רבי יהושע בן לוי: Why did they say that the morning prayer lasts until noon? Because the morning daily offering may be brought until noon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the promised support for רבי יהושע בן לוי. The ברייתא explains a prayer deadline by matching it to the daily offering’s deadline.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question introduces the reason for the stated prayer time. The answer uses the morning תָּמִיד to explain why that time ends at noon.

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: And it was taught in support of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הַשַּׁחַר עַד חֲצוֹת —
phrases.english: Why did they say that the morning prayer lasts until noon?
Because the daily morning offering
may be offered until noon.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the source about the אבות, the גמרא presents the source for the view about the תְּמִידִין.
steps.raayaObject: The link between the time for morning prayer and the time for the morning תָּמִיד.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא gives the morning תָּמִיד’s noon endpoint as the reason for the prayer’s noon endpoint.

steps.title: An earlier endpoint also follows the offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives an earlier endpoint for morning prayer and likewise bases it on the morning תָּמִיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the morning prayer lasts until four hours into the day, because the daily morning offering may be brought until four hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds רבי יהודה’s different deadline. It gives the same kind of reason: the prayer time follows the offering time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stated deadline changes from noon to four hours. What stays the same is the way the deadline is explained—through the morning תָּמִיד.

keyTerms.meaning: The sage who gives the earlier endpoint here.
Continues to be eligible to be offered.

steps.whatToRemember: This ברייתא supports the link proposed by רבי יהושע בן לוי: even when the stated deadline differs, the explanation for prayer time comes from the time of the תָּמִיד.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda says: Until four hours into the day,
because the daily morning offering
may be offered until four hours into the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא adds רבי יהודה’s earlier endpoint while continuing to explain prayer time through the תָּמִיד.
steps.raayaObject: The offering-based explanation of רבי יהודה’s four-hour endpoint for morning prayer.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא says that the morning תָּמִיד may be brought until four hours into the day.

steps.title: Why the afternoon prayer lasts until evening
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא links the end time for מנחה to the afternoon תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say that מנחה lasts until evening? Because the afternoon תמיד continued to be offered until evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now turns from שחרית to מנחה. It gives the afternoon תמיד as the reason for the stated end time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same pattern used for שחרית continues: the prayer’s time follows its corresponding offering. Here, that gives מנחה an endpoint of evening.

phrases.english: And why did they say that the afternoon prayer
lasts until evening? Because
the daily afternoon offering
continued to be offered until evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הַמִּנְחָה עַד הָעֶרֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא’s explanation of prayer endpoints, moving from שחרית to מנחה.
steps.raayaObject: The endpoint of מנחה at evening.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The time of the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה gives an earlier afternoon endpoint
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה ties his earlier endpoint for מנחה to the afternoon תמיד as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Until the midpoint of the מנחה period, because the afternoon תמיד continued to be offered until that midpoint.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה’s different endpoint for מנחה and its reason. This is a second view of the same prayer time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not switch to a different offering. He uses the afternoon תמיד too, but connects מנחה to an earlier endpoint.

keyTerms.meaning: the sage giving the earlier endpoint
the midpoint of the מנחה period

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until the midpoint of the afternoon period,
because the daily afternoon offering
continued to be offered until the midpoint of the afternoon period.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה’s different endpoint for the same prayer.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה’s endpoint for מנחה at פלג המנחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The stated endpoint of the afternoon תמיד.

steps.title: Why the evening prayer has no fixed time
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא connects ערבית to offering parts that continued burning through the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say that the evening prayer has no fixed time? Because limbs and fats not consumed by evening continued to be offered throughout the night.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to ערבית and explains its nighttime timing. It points to parts of offerings that remained to be burned after evening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connection differs from the daytime prayers: it points to an activity continuing through the night, not to a newly brought daily offering. That explains the wording אין לה קבע here.

keyTerms.meaning: were consumed by the altar fire

phrases.english: And why did they say that the evening prayer
has no fixed time? Because
limbs and fats that had not been consumed by evening
continued to be offered throughout the night.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ תְּפִלַּת הָעֶרֶב אֵין לָהּ קֶבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the two endpoints for מנחה to the timing of ערבית.
steps.raayaObject: The stated absence of a fixed time for ערבית.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The overnight burning of limbs and fats left from offerings.

steps.title: Why מוסף lasts all day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא connects the full-day time for מוסף to the מוסף offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they say that the additional prayer lasts all day? Because the additional offering could be brought all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא next explains the stated time for מוסף. It again matches the prayer’s time to its offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The offering named here is קרבן מוסף. Its stated full-day time provides the reason for the full-day time given to the prayer.

phrases.english: And why did they say that the additional prayer
lasts all day? Because

phrases.aramaic: קׇרְבָּן שֶׁל מוּסָפִין קָרֵב כׇּל הַיּוֹם.
phrases.english: the additional offering could be brought all day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרוּ שֶׁל מוּסָפִין כׇּל הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the offering-based explanations, now for מוסף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The full-day time of the מוסף offering.

steps.title: Why רבי יהודה ends מוסף earlier
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה gives מוסף an endpoint at seven hours and links it to the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Until seven hours, because the additional offering continued to be brought until seven hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהודה’s different endpoint for מוסף. It supplies a reason from the מוסף offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference from the previous step is the endpoint: seven hours instead of all day. The method stays the same—the prayer’s time is tied to the offering’s time.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Until seven hours,
because the additional offering
continued to be brought until seven hours.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁבַע שָׁעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה’s different endpoint for the מוסף time just explained.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה’s seven-hour endpoint for מוסף.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The stated seven-hour endpoint of the מוסף offering.

steps.title: Defining מנחה גדולה and מנחה קטנה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines when מנחה גדולה and מנחה קטנה begin.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the greater afternoon period? From six and a half hours onward. And what is the smaller afternoon period? From nine and a half hours onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now pauses to define two time labels used for מנחה. It gives the starting point of each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחה גדולה begins at six and a half hours; מנחה קטנה begins at nine and a half hours. These are definitions of the two periods, not new explanations for the prayer’s endpoint.

keyTerms.meaning: from six and a half hours
from nine and a half hours

steps.whatToRemember: מנחה גדולה starts at six and a half hours; מנחה קטנה starts at nine and a half hours.

phrases.english: And what is the greater afternoon period?
From six and a half hours onward.
And what is the smaller afternoon period?
From nine and a half hours onward.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא מִנְחָה גְדוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from מוסף to clarify two terms for afternoon times.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מנחה גדולה starts at six and a half hours, and מנחה קטנה starts at nine and a half hours.

steps.title: Which half of the afternoon does he mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which afternoon period רבי יהודה divides in half.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: When רבי יהודה says the midpoint of מנחה, does he mean the first מנחה period or the later מנחה period?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא needs to pin down רבי יהודה’s endpoint for מנחה. This question sets up a source that will identify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase “half of מנחה” is not precise enough by itself. The two possibilities give different times.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was raised for them
the midpoint of the first מנחה period
the midpoint of the later מנחה period

phrases.english: A question was raised for them: Rabbi Yehuda—
does he mean the midpoint of the first minḥa period,
or does he mean the midpoint of the later minḥa period?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 19 defined the two מנחה periods; this step asks which one רבי יהודה means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which מנחה period is divided to produce רבי יהודה’s endpoint?

steps.title: The later afternoon period is meant
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states that רבי יהודה means the midpoint of the later מנחה period and gives its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A teaching states that רבי יהודה means the midpoint of the later afternoon period. That time is eleven hours minus a quarter-hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an explicit ברייתא to answer the question. It names the later מנחה period and gives the clock time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא removes the uncertainty about which period to halve. Its stated time is ten and three-quarter hours into the day.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear; an introduction to a source
as it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says,
They meant the midpoint of the later minḥa period,

phrases.aramaic: וְהִיא אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁעוֹת חָסֵר רְבִיעַ.
phrases.english: and it is eleven hours minus a quarter.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the choice posed in step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה means the midpoint of the later מנחה period: ten and three-quarter hours into the day.

steps.title: Does the offerings connection refute the other view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the link between prayer times and offerings defeats רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא’s account of who instituted prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we say that this refutes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns from the exact time to a broader challenge. It asks whether the offerings-based timing contradicts רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier sources connected prayer times to offerings. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the אבות instituted the prayers, so the גמרא tests whether those two claims can fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: let this be a refutation of his view
the sage whose account of prayer’s institution is being challenged

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation
of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא תֶּיהְוֵי תְּיוּבְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the timing question, the גמרא tests what the offerings connections imply about prayer’s origin.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא that the אבות instituted the prayers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If prayer times are tied to offerings, perhaps offerings—not the אבות—must be their source.

steps.title: The prayers’ origin and their timing can differ
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא’s view is defended: the אבות instituted the prayers, while the חכמים aligned them with offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא could answer: The אבות instituted the prayers, and the חכמים linked them to the offerings. Otherwise, who instituted תפילת מוסף? Therefore, these two accounts must work together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating who instituted the prayers from how their times were set. It uses תפילת מוסף to show why the account needs both parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבות can be the source of the regular prayers even though the חכמים linked prayer practice to offerings. תפילת מוסף has no matching prayer instituted by an individual ancestor, making the offerings connection necessary in this account.

keyTerms.meaning: and the חכמים linked them to the קרבנות

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, could say to you:
I can still say to you that the prayers—
the Patriarchs instituted them, and the Sages linked them to the offerings.
For if you do not say this,

phrases.aramaic: תְּפִלַּת מוּסָף לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
phrases.english: the additional prayer, according to Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina—
who instituted it?
Rather, the Patriarchs instituted the prayers,
and the Sages linked them to the offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It rejects the proposed refutation by showing that institution and offerings-based timing are compatible.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the origin of the prayers from the later linking of their practice to offerings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An offerings connection would rule out the claim that the אבות instituted prayer.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אבות instituted the prayers, and the חכמים linked them to offerings.
steps.whyThisMatters: This lets the sugya retain both explanations without treating them as competing answers to exactly the same question.

steps.title: Does “until four hours” include the fourth hour?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה’s morning-prayer endpoint and asks whether עד includes that hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: until four hours. They asked: Does “until” include the endpoint, or does it exclude the endpoint?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new timing question about תפילת שחרית. It asks exactly how to read רבי יהודה’s word עד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the endpoint is included, the fourth hour is available. If it is excluded, the fourth hour is not available under רבי יהודה’s limit.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: until four hours.
They asked: Does “until” include the endpoint,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא עַד וְלֹא עַד בַּכְּלָל?!
phrases.english: or perhaps does “until” not include the endpoint?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר עַד אַרְבַּע שָׁעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion leaves the origin of prayer and begins a separate question about the wording of a time limit.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does עד include or exclude the fourth hour in רבי יהודה’s limit for תפילת שחרית?

steps.title: Test “until” against the afternoon limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins testing the meaning of עד using רבי יהודה’s limit for מנחה. The argument continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says, “until the midpoint of the afternoon.” If “until” excludes its endpoint, the difference between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is understandable. But if “until” includes its endpoint, רבי יהודה—
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יהודה’s מנחה wording to test the new question. It starts comparing the two readings of עד, but the source stops mid-argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading—excluding the endpoint—is presented as fitting a difference between רבי יהודה and the חכמים. The גמרא then begins to test the inclusive reading, but its reason is not yet given here.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says,
until the midpoint of the afternoon.
Granted, if you say
“until” does not include the endpoint—

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיכָּא בֵּין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: then there is a difference between Rabbi Yehuda and the Sages.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ עַד וְעַד בַּכְּלָל,
phrases.english: But if you say “until” includes the endpoint,
Rabbi Yehuda—

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד פְּלַג הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It begins an attempted proof about the meaning of עד from רבי יהודה’s wording for מנחה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether עד includes its stated endpoint.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה’s statement that מנחה extends עד פלג המנחה.
